title: Neonatal mortality rate
national_indicator_description: The probability of dying within the first month of life, based on the number of deaths during the first 28 completed days of life per 1000 live births in the reference period.
computation_definitions: Probability that a child born alive in a specified period will die during the first 28 completed days of life if subject to age-specific mortality rates of that period.
computation_calculations: (Number of deaths of infants (<28 days) in the reference period / Total number of live births in the reference period) * 1000
other_info: Figures for the total under-5 mortality rate, as well as breakdowns by sex and urban/rural residence for 2020 and 2025, are calculated based on the 5-year period preceding the survey; breakdowns by sex and urban/rural residence for 2008, 2010, and 2015, as well as all breakdowns by province, are calculated based on the 10-year period preceding the survey. Note that breakdowns from different periods cannot be directly compared. For more details, see the linked data source. Alternative estimates of the neonatal mortality rate developed by the World Health Organization (WHO) can be found on the [WHO Data Portal](https://data.who.int/indicators/i/E3CAF2B/A4C49D3?m49=646).
comments_limitations: Figures from the Demographic and Health Survey are subject to recall error. Interviewed women may omit births and deaths or include stillbirths along with live births. Survey data may also suffer from survivor selection bias and age truncation. Mothers may misreport their children’s birth dates, current ages or ages at death, perhaps more so if the child has died. For more details on limitations, see the linked data source.
indicator_definition: Probability that a child born in a specific year or period will die during the first 28 completed days of life if subject to age-specific mortality rates of that period, expressed per 1000 live births. Neonatal deaths (deaths among live births during the first 28 completed days of life) may be subdivided into early neonatal deaths, occurring during the first 7 days of life, and late neonatal deaths, occurring after the 7th day but before the 28th completed day of life.
